author: hey1tspriyanshu
quote: i tried logging into verizon through grok and through muse and it simply won’t. “this page isn’t available right now.” even when the egress was supposed to be through my own computer.
summary: User tried to log in to the Verizon account portal with Grok Bot and with Meta Muse; the portal refused both, and a basic CAPTCHA stopped the agent.

author: hey1tspriyanshu
quote: facebook told me something signed in near flower mound — chrome on linux — while i’m in connecticut. i want that email.
summary: Grok Bot and Muse signed in to Facebook from a cloud browser; Facebook sent a new-device security alert and the session did not stay active.

author: hey1tspriyanshu
quote: ebay pinging new devices from chicago / fort worth / london? also fine. that’s my account.
summary: Agent sessions on eBay came from different cities; eBay sent new-device alerts and the sessions did not stay active.

author: nabeel_sajid97
quote: 1000+ scraper requests per second. Someone had figured out our Cloudflare security check.
summary: Site owner put Cloudflare in front of the site because of scrapers; a developer's API calls got 403 errors, and later an AI-made script defeated the Cloudflare check at 1000+ requests per second.

author: capitaltruist
quote: buying 90% of new stuff, aside from when it's blocked by captcha
summary: User buys most new items through the Instinct agent; purchases fail when a CAPTCHA blocks the agent.

author: capitaltruist
quote: It signed up completely by itself and created docs, added folders, sent me screenshots of its progress. @falconer_ai was built for an agent-friendly world, and the pairing is magical.
summary: Instinct used its own email address to sign up to Falconer without help, then made docs and folders for a knowledge base.

author: Surajit03653424
quote: If an SMS OTP or CAPTCHA pops up, the agent pauses and prompts me directly in the CLI
summary: Builder made a DeepSeek + Playwright agent that fills sign-up forms; it stops and asks the human when an SMS OTP or CAPTCHA shows.

author: dlimeng192048
quote: But the site still sees a datacenter IP, causing captchas, 403s or blocks, and some internal systems only allow company fixed IPs.
summary: Description of Grok Bot: the user takes control to log in, but sites see a datacenter IP and show CAPTCHAs or 403s; traffic through the user's own computer removes this.

author: cosmoene
quote: Blocking should be a switch the owner reaches for, not the position they start in.
summary: Opinion on the Cloudflare default of 15 September 2026: new domains block agent and training bots on pages with ads, thus owners lose agent traffic and did not decide it.

author: mykcaron
quote: On pages that display ads, Training and Agent are now blocked by default; Search stays allowed. It applies to new domains and to every free customer who changed nothing.
summary: Explanation of the Cloudflare policy: bots in the Agent class are blocked by default on pages with ads, also for a services site with an old AdSense tag.

author: OPuzanov
quote: a default config gets you flagged by Cloudflare in under 60 seconds. Headless flags, matching canvas fingerprints, and datacenter IP ranges are dead giveaways.
summary: Builder reports that default Playwright or Puppeteer automation gets a 90%+ block rate on sites with Cloudflare bot management.

author: claytoncollie
quote: And they have to make it much easier to spin up a fresh WordPress site programmatically.
summary: Opinion that an agent cannot easily make a new WordPress site by program, because hosting providers do not supply the path.

author: claytoncollie
quote: It is so easy to deploy a site to vercel or cloudflare with an agent. Should be the same for WordPress.
summary: Agents deploy a site to Vercel easily.

author: claytoncollie
quote: It is so easy to deploy a site to vercel or cloudflare with an agent. Should be the same for WordPress.
summary: Agents deploy a site to Cloudflare easily.

author: Surajit03653424
quote: Websites use multi-stage forms, dynamically rendered elements, custom consent controls, CAPTCHAs, and validation rules that can silently reject an action.
summary: Builder of a general sign-up agent lists what breaks sign-up flows: multi-stage forms, dynamic elements, consent controls, CAPTCHAs and silent validation rejects.

author: im_thejas
quote: Have to work on that, thanks for the score @Cloudflare, will make the website agent ready!
summary: Site owner got an agent-readiness score from the Cloudflare tool and plans to make the site agent-ready.

author: KJChizzy
quote: MCP support (local + cloudflare worker), llms.txt, public OpenAPI + JSON catalog APIs so agents can actually read the site instead of scraping it.
summary: Site owner released MCP, llms.txt and public catalog APIs so that agents read the site and do not scrape it.

author: itsabhisheksood
quote: It used it's own browser and failed as it can't solve the captcha... It can't even natively use the 2captcha or any api key..
summary: Grok Bot tried to submit business citations on directory sites and failed at the CAPTCHA; the user had Claude Code build a proxy browser MCP as a workaround.

author: 256BitChris
quote: A lot of websites are blocking your LLMs from accessing - returning 403s or other errors. This is super annoying and causes your LLM to have to guess for answers
summary: Claude and Codex get 403 errors from many websites during research; the user sends requests through the ScrapingBee API as a workaround.

author: leadgenjay
quote: Deploy Hermes Agent on Hetzner VPS via Claude Code — no dashboard logins needed
summary: Claude Code deployed an agent to a Hetzner VPS with no dashboard login.

author: leadgenjay
quote: Connect apps via Composio (OAuth handled automatically)
summary: User connected the agent to apps through Composio, which did the OAuth flows automatically.

author: kyle_fowler2
quote: You have a solution for when codex needs to login to something that has a password? I use codex running remotely on a Mac mini for everything but this is one of the most annoying problems I run into
summary: User runs Codex remotely on a Mac mini; password logins on websites stop it again and again.

author: chandnirao_here
quote: Instinct: easy authentication to ue (link to email), quick search for items, cart addition, hands the final cart back to me to review (i asked for it)
summary: Instinct connected to Uber Eats through an email link, found items, filled the cart and gave the cart to the user for review.

author: chandnirao_here
quote: Muse: - can't connect to uber eats so sorry - asks for postal code - opens ue in browser - needs verification code for sign-in - blocked by CAPTCHA - hands the task back to me??
summary: Meta Muse could not connect to Uber Eats; in the browser it needed a sign-in verification code, then a CAPTCHA blocked it and it gave the task back.

author: ohad_maimon
quote: Instinct's agent can read your texts, pick up the 2FA code and complete the flow.
summary: Observer reports that Instinct reads the SMS 2FA code from the user's texts and completes the flow; the writer sees a trust risk for agentic payments.

author: TylerM
quote: constantly being prompted for a 2fa token that times out by the time i get it to them is horrible ux
summary: User of Instinct, Muse and Grok Bot: agents ask for 2FA tokens again and again, and the token expires before the user can send it.

author: DonizetiFerre16
quote: stage-only granular tokens can submit a package version for review but can’t publish it directly.
summary: npm stage-only tokens let a release agent prepare a package version while a maintainer keeps the publish step behind 2FA.

author: somi_ai
quote: most agents still can't get past my email's 2FA without me babysitting it
summary: User says agents cannot pass the 2FA on the user's email account without help.

author: radardigital_ai
quote: A new analysis found restrictions on cart or checkout paths at 15 of 18 major retailers, while 6 of 20 sites directly rejected ChatGPT-User traffic.
summary: Analysis of major US e-commerce sites: most restrict cart or checkout paths for agents, and 6 of 20 reject ChatGPT-User traffic.

author: michaelquoc
quote: as more and more shopping is handled by agents, bot clicks will no longer be valueless. They may actually reflect purchase intent by human operators.
summary: Opinion for store owners: the Cloudflare default blocks shopping agents on pages with ads, but agent visits can carry purchase intent.

author: KamilZonesmart
quote: ChatGPT Instant Checkout is gone. Walmart: in-chat buys converted at 1/3 of click-out. Retired in March.
summary: Report that Walmart purchases in ChatGPT Instant Checkout converted at one third of the click-out rate, and that the feature was retired in March 2026.

author: alexcrdean
quote: it's more nuanced now than ban/block. Some of the highest-value users now are experimenting with agent computer use, Instinct etc
summary: Analytics vendor tells site owners that block-all is wrong now, because high-value users come through agents such as Instinct.

author: alexgroberman
quote: Some site owners are going to misunderstand what is happening and play this wrong
summary: Advice to site owners: the new Cloudflare Disallow AI Training setting blocks training and keeps search crawlers, so owners stay visible in AI assistants.

author: PujaraMihir
quote: february, forrester counted about 30 actually live. march, instant checkout got reframed as moving to apps. walmart measured in chat converting roughly 3x worse than sending people to their own site.
summary: One-year review of ChatGPT agentic checkout: about 30 merchants live, Walmart in-chat conversion about 3x worse; discovery worked and checkout did not.

author: yannis1kiefer
quote: agentic checkout blanked our pixel once and we spent a week guessing.
summary: Merchant reports that an agentic checkout (Muse with Stripe Link) removed the attribution pixel data, and the team could not find the source of sales for a week.

author: avthar
quote: Love Cloudflare. Use their MCP / plugins for Codex and Claude Code. Experience is delightful and very cost efficient as well.
summary: User operates Cloudflare through its MCP server and plugins for Codex and Claude Code and reports a very good experience.

author: ecooai
quote: with cloudflare mcp, you can build webapp directly in chat mode , no codex and work mode need
summary: User built and deployed a full chat web app from the ChatGPT chat UI through the Cloudflare MCP server.

author: altryne
quote: Service account with agents own vault
summary: User names the 1Password service account with a vault for the agent as the best feature for agent credential access.

author: mdlahfir
quote: In this video, using WebMCP, i selected a seat, entered details, and booked all in three tool calls.
summary: Builder made a test flight seat-selection iframe with WebMCP tools; the agent selected a seat and booked in three tool calls, with no screenshot loop.

author: itscjzhao
quote: untrustedContentHint and consequentialHint went unused across all 8 — not because they didn't apply, but because I couldn't tell what declaring them would change.
summary: Implementer shipped 8 WebMCP tools in an enterprise workflow product and used only readOnlyHint, because the effect of the other hints is not clear.

author: pridgenmd
quote: Currently, subagents don’t seem to share that page access, so their tool calls aren’t reaching the active page.
summary: Tester of Codex Voice on a WebMCP page: delegated subagents do not get the live page, so their WebMCP tool calls fail.

author: harshpatel071
quote: in the video a refund on an unpaid invoice gets rejected. agent or human, doesn't matter.
summary: Product builder registers screen actions as WebMCP tools; an agent refund on an unpaid invoice got the same validation reject as a human click.

author: f0rr0
quote: Namefi now has a remote MCP and WebMCP. We share some of the underlying contracts to keep things clean and consistent. Also using the newly added consequential hint to flag critical DNS record updates.
summary: Namefi released a remote MCP server and WebMCP with shared contracts, and uses the consequential hint for critical DNS record changes.

author: nucliweb
quote: An agent shouldn't have to guess CSS selectors to read a conference schedule. I implemented WebMCP on the GeeksCAT Conf 2026 website: a static Astro site, no server.
summary: Site owner added WebMCP to a static Astro conference site so that agents read the schedule without CSS selectors.

author: sebuzdugan
quote: what happens when webmcp descriptions drift from the ui? agents fail more confidently than before
summary: Concern from a developer: when WebMCP tool descriptions and the UI become different, agents fail with more confidence.

author: ApogeeIS
quote: an agent that aims at a button which then jumps mid-click fails even when WebMCP and the accessibility tree look fine.
summary: Performance specialist: late layout shift moves a button during the agent click, and the click fails although WebMCP and the accessibility tree are correct.

author: ondakx
quote: Only downside for me is auth and sometimes when mcp could not authenticate cli was just better?
summary: User has used MCP servers for a year with success; authentication is the weak point, and a CLI worked better when the MCP could not authenticate.

author: LottieFiles
quote: With ChatGPT + WebMCP + Lottie Creator → a real editable Lottie animation. Same prompt. Production-ready output.
summary: Lottie Creator added WebMCP; ChatGPT operates the editor through tools and makes an editable animation.

author: prd_008
quote: it's like Overcooked, but you use the keyboard and your agent uses WebMCP.
summary: Builder made a co-op browser game where the human uses the keyboard and the ChatGPT agent acts through WebMCP tools on the same page.

author: TheRealTechCPA
quote: I’ve noticed computer use and the virtual browser to basically be so good in Astra, I wonder if there’s still as much utility in webMCP?
summary: User finds computer use in the ChatGPT Astra virtual browser good, and doubts that WebMCP adds much for strong models.

author: JackyXP111
quote: We have been dispatching agents to test out merchant's storefronts, less than 20% passing rate to checkout.
summary: Team sent agents to test merchant storefronts; less than 20% of the runs got to checkout.

author: pk_iv
quote: your agent can now natively make payments on the web using link cli + browserbase.
summary: Browserbase reports that an agent pays on web checkouts with the Stripe Link CLI and a Browserbase browser from a one-shot prompt.

author: gareth_w
quote: The bot couldn’t click “Place order” and asked me to try on its computer. I couldn’t get it to work either.
summary: Grok Bot got to checkout but could not click Place order; the user also failed on the bot computer during a Grok Bot incident.

author: blue_eyes_0928
quote: One-tap Squarespace checkout almost cost me ~$400 and delayed launch: $186.18 charged, site still on trial, wrong account path.
summary: A one-tap Squarespace checkout charged the wrong account path; Grok Bot made the evidence pack and stayed in the support case until the refund.

author: galengidman
quote: How do you keep your Grok Bots from getting stopped by every Cloudflare and CAPTCHA to the point of being unusable for travel research/booking?
summary: User says Cloudflare checks and CAPTCHAs stop Grok Bot so frequently that travel research and booking is not usable.

author: kr0der
quote: my Grok Bot was stuck on a Cloudflare captcha on its desktop this allowed it to access the site via my computer instead
summary: Grok Bot stopped at a Cloudflare CAPTCHA on its cloud desktop; the user made a route through the user's own computer and the site opened.

author: pupsierra
quote: Anyone else having issues with the Costco website sign in form not working in Grok Bot?
summary: The Costco sign-in form did not work in the Grok Bot browser.

author: pupsierra
quote: Walmart and Target worked fine after I did the CAPTCHA for them.
summary: Walmart worked in Grok Bot after the user solved the CAPTCHA.

author: pupsierra
quote: Walmart and Target worked fine after I did the CAPTCHA for them.
summary: Target worked in Grok Bot after the user solved the CAPTCHA.

author: QINGCHARLES
quote: Grok wrote me a nice CAPTCHA bypass for a site that was annoying me the other day. I tried to get Claude and Codex to do it, but they refused.
summary: A site CAPTCHA blocked the user; Grok wrote a bypass, while Claude and Codex refused the task.

author: ManningDrakeOG
quote: The agents have had a difficult time logging into some of our portals as the cyber security recognizes they aren’t human after they use our logins.
summary: Company started Grok Bot on its work portals; portal security detects the bots after login, and the bot passed about half of the CAPTCHA gates.

author: maestrooth
quote: the cloud computer trips site security. X will lock the login
summary: Community list of Grok Bot problems: the cloud computer triggers site security, and X locks the login.

author: AswinDigital
quote: Best Buy: live browser ERR_HTTP2_PROTOCOL_ERROR; page-reader 503 / country-selector.
summary: Grok Bot price comparison log: Best Buy gave a protocol error in the live browser and 503 in the page reader; the price came from an indexed page.

author: AswinDigital
quote: Walmart: first load hit a “Press & Hold” bot check; product details then retrieved via page reader.
summary: Grok Bot price comparison log: Walmart showed a Press & Hold bot check, then the page reader got the product details.

author: AswinDigital
quote: B&H: Cloudflare “Verify you are human” — no live price.
summary: Grok Bot price comparison log: B&H showed the Cloudflare human check and the bot got no live price.

author: AswinDigital
quote: Live-extracted: Amazon $29.99, Choice badge, Prime/stock/ratings/specs
summary: Grok Bot price comparison log: Amazon product data (price, badge, stock, ratings) came from the live page with no block.

author: BrianCLowe
quote: @bot was blocked from browsing a store's site in Chrome. Switched to Brave on the box and Brave's privacy features actually let me pay.
summary: A store site blocked Grok Bot in Chrome; the user changed to the Brave browser on the bot computer and the payment went through.

author: uniquesupri
quote: Grok bot worked quite well with many usecases except with https://t.co/SJpGPRzKIN and Tesla website. Both blocked the bot usage. Ironic.
summary: Grok Bot worked on many sites, but x.com blocked it.

author: uniquesupri
quote: Grok bot worked quite well with many usecases except with https://t.co/SJpGPRzKIN and Tesla website. Both blocked the bot usage. Ironic.
summary: Grok Bot worked on many sites, but the Tesla website blocked it.

author: cyberbeast_fl
quote: You couldn't even access the Tesla website on Grok Bot to look up car prices before!
summary: User reports that Grok Bot could not open the Tesla website to read car prices, and welcomes a fix.

author: vigram_void
quote: @grok access @X but every other agents are blocked
summary: User complains that X permits only Grok and blocks all other agents for data collection.

author: vigram_void
quote: @ChatGPT access @LinkedIn but every other agents are blocked! @claudeai has access to no socials!
summary: User complains that LinkedIn permits only ChatGPT and blocks other agents; Claude gets no social sites.
